name: Dirty Frag post-compromise attack graph
summary: Defensive attack path model for Dirty Frag local privilege escalation from an existing Linux foothold to root-level objectives.

nodes.label: Initial low-privileged foothold
nodes.description: Adversary gains or already has low-privileged local execution through SSH, web shell, service account, CI runner, or container workload.
evidence: Container shell or service account execution

nodes.label: Interactive shell and host discovery
nodes.description: Actor uses shell commands to identify kernel version, user context, writable directories, and candidate escalation paths.

nodes.label: Dirty Frag-relevant module exposure
nodes.description: Host has esp4, esp6, rxrpc, or related networking functionality loaded or loadable and has not yet been remediated by a vendor kernel update.
evidence: Kernel module object exists on disk
No modprobe block rule for unused affected modules

nodes.label: Local exploit artifact staged
nodes.description: Actor writes and executes a local ELF-style artifact from a writable path. Microsoft reported an observed artifact named ./update, but names are easily changed.
evidence: New executable in /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, web roots, or /run/user
Execution of ./update or similarly named local binary

nodes.label: Dirty Frag local privilege escalation attempt
nodes.description: Existing local foothold attempts to abuse Dirty Frag kernel behavior to transition from low privilege to root. This graph deliberately does not encode exploit mechanics.
evidence: Suspicious local binary execution followed by root transition
Unexpected root-owned child process from low-privileged session

nodes.label: Root context obtained
nodes.description: Actor obtains UID 0 context and can alter host state, disable controls, or access sensitive application data.
evidence: Root-owned process tree after low-privileged staging

nodes.label: GLPI and PHP session tampering
nodes.description: Actor modifies GLPI-related authentication files or deletes/wipes PHP session files to remove evidence or affect application access.
evidence: Vim swap files in GLPI paths

nodes.label: Credential and sensitive data access
nodes.description: Root context allows access to application configuration, session data, local credentials, tokens, and other sensitive host data.
evidence: Reads of app configuration and session files
Access to secrets, tokens, or LDAP configuration
Unusual root reads from service directories

nodes.label: Patch and module controls
nodes.description: Vendor kernel remediation, reboot compliance, and disabling unused esp4, esp6, or rxrpc modules reduce the attack path.
evidence: Remediated kernel package installed and booted
Business owner validation for IPsec/RxRPC usage

nodes.label: Hunting and response analytics
nodes.description: KQL, Sigma, osquery, and PoC artifacts in this repository provide behavior hunting, exposure checks, and triage leads.

edges.label: patching and module policy reduce exposure
staging hunts detect suspicious local artifact execution
file hunts detect GLPI/PHP session tampering
PoC and osquery detect module exposure
